purpose: The whole looks Spider-Bot as one assembly: the parametric legs (8), eyes, base and body placed with cad/motion.py, and the drive fitted inside them: N10 gear motor, gear train to the crankshafts, 6 x AG13 wired 2S3P with contacts, slide switch, two 5 mm LED eye bores. The scale S is 1.0 (Morante, 2026-11-26: «S 1.0 máximo»): every length in cad/motion.py P0 (approved at N0 at 0.60) times S/0.60, so the look is N0's; printable minimums wall 2.0, gear module 1.0, M3.
pass_criterion: full cad_verify PASS with every part inside (no collision over the 24 poses, each part's assembly path) at the chosen S, and the judge >= 0.60 against jenscolt's model (his photos and his assembled meshes in the same views as the robot)
must_have: the parts are imported from cad/legs, cad/eyes, cad/base, cad/body; scale, crank and leg path from cad/motion.py, never copied
the parametric parts may be reshaped where the inside needs it (surfaces moved, stretched or opened), as long as the robot's look passes the judge

every part, screw and contact is in the code that counts the fit; a fit that leaves something out is reported as partial. Wires take no volume (flexible, routed by hand); only a hole or slot where a wire must pass a wall between its two ends (Morante, 2026-11-21: «no consideres los cables ni el espacio que ocupan… si hay que conectar cables entre dos puntos que separa una pared, sí tienes que dejar un agujero o ranura para que pasen»)
assembly order and each part's path checked before the scale
the motor's fit is a separate, screwed part (the motor is bought later and measured; a fix reprints grams)
Morante can change the cells; the switch is reached from outside
two 5 mm LED bores in the eyes, wired by Morante (no eyes board)
the views command renders the robot and jenscolt's assembled meshes in the same views and framing, written as images/reference.png next to the photos
fasteners: M3 everywhere (holes fits.STEEL on Ø3.3), or snap fits (datasheet robot «Phase 1 result», Morante 2026-11-26)
margins, walls and clearances: the standard values of cad/fits.py; changed only where they cause a problem, and put to Morante
print support as little as possible; up to 20-30 % on a part is accepted when a valid solution needs it
screwdriver access: where it blocks a solution, it is put to Morante before the solution is dropped

when something collides: first layout; then the colliding part is reshaped locally to make room (a pocket, relief, notch or bulge), any bulge outward on the shell (base) or the body first; a larger S is not wanted and is only put to Morante when nothing else works (Morante, 2026-11-21: «cada vez que te encuentres con un problema de colisiones, modifica o deforma la pieza local para dar cabida a lo que falta… empiezas por fuera en la carcasa o en el cuerpo»; «no quiero aumentar la escala más»)

views.py places jenscolt's meshes (body, base, eyes, sensor, 8 legs; leg placement as the archived tools/assemble_jenscolt.py) at the robot's S and frame, writes out/reference.stl, and renders robot and reference with tools/mesh_ref.py views; `views.py --reference` writes images/reference.png; meshes are read only here, never by build.py or a gate
cell contacts: conical springs + nickel strip (to buy)
eye LEDs: red or yellow from the Arduino kit, with their resistors placed and counted
wiring through one 3-pin JST-XH (to buy); hook-up wire from the Arduino kit
body held at the front by snap fits (the front screws are boxed in by the eye block and the legs); screws only where they have driver access (Morante, 2026-11-21: «Ok»)
must_not: a probe that leaves parts out reported as a fit
jenscolt's inner posts in the body or base

S_start.source: Morante 2026-11-26: «S 1.0 máximo»; motion.py lengths × S/0.60, printed layout numbers set at 0.70 × S/0.70, fits never scaled

motor_n10.source: nominal micro metal gear motor N10 (motor 12 + gearbox 9 mm); not bought: to be measured on arrival (hardware.md)

led.source: Morante, 2026-11-19: two 5 mm LEDs from the Arduino kit, eye bores only

support_max.source: Morante, 2026-11-20: as little as possible; 20-30 % accepted when a valid solution needs it

hookup_wire_od.source: Morante, 2026-11-21: «Asume 1 mm», cannot measure it; kit hook-up wire (22-24 AWG) is often 1.4-1.6, so the routes also report their margin at 1.6; used only to size the holes/slots where a wire passes a wall

references.label: jenscolt's assembled meshes, same views and framing as the robot
